# datadog_rum_operation (Resource)

Provides a Datadog RUM Operation resource. This can be used to create and manage RUM operations. When automatic SLO creation is enabled for the organization, creating an operation also creates an availability SLO tagged `feature_operation:<name>`, and deleting it deletes the SLOs carrying that tag for the operation's application. Renaming the operation or changing its application leaves the previous SLO in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "datadog_rum_operation" "checkout" {
  name           = "checkout"
  display_name   = "Checkout"
  application_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  description    = "From the cart to the order confirmation page."
  category       = "form_submission"
  tags           = ["team:payments"]

  steps = [
    {
      type  = "start"
      nodes = [{ query = "@view.name:/cart @action.name:checkout" }]
    },
    {
      type  = "stop"
      nodes = [{ query = "@view.name:/order/confirmation" }]
    },
    {
      type = "error"
      composite = {
        kind          = "in_order"
        max_window_ms = 60000
        predicates = [
          { query = "@type:action @action.name:pay" },
          { query = "@type:error @error.message:*declined*" },
        ]
      }
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `application_id` (String) ID of the RUM application the operation belongs to.
- `name` (String) Unique name of the operation within the organization. Must not contain spaces. Changing it recreates the operation.
- `steps` (Attributes List) Ordered steps defining how RUM events drive the operation lifecycle. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps))

### Optional

- `category` (String) Category of the operation.
- `description` (String) Description of the operation.
- `display_name` (String) Human readable name of the operation. Defaults to `name`.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags attached to the operation.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--steps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `steps`

Required:

- `type` (String) Lifecycle transition triggered by this step. Valid values are `start`, `update`, `stop`, `error`, `abandoned`.

Optional:

- `composite` (Attributes) Rule combining several predicates into this step. Exactly one of `nodes` or `composite` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps--composite))
- `nodes` (Attributes List) Queries matched by this step. Exactly one of `nodes` or `composite` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps--nodes))

<a id="nestedatt--steps--composite"></a>
### Nested Schema for `steps.composite`

Required:

- `kind` (String) How the predicates combine. Valid values are `all_of`, `in_order`.
- `predicates` (Attributes List) Predicates combined by the rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps--composite--predicates))

Optional:

- `max_window_ms` (Number) Maximum time window, in milliseconds, in which all predicates must match. Value must be between 0 and 1800000.

<a id="nestedatt--steps--composite--predicates"></a>
### Nested Schema for `steps.composite.predicates`

Required:

- `query` (String) RUM event search query.



<a id="nestedatt--steps--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `steps.nodes`

Required:

- `query` (String) RUM event search query.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import datadog_rum_operation.checkout "<operation_id>"
```
